newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends higher on China demand, meal up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends higher on China demand, meal up.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed firm in the nearby months on news China was buying U.S. soyoil, traders said.
"There was talk about China oil business," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
U.S. exporters said China bought at least 44,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil for prompt shipment and some estimated Chinese purchases this week at up to 70,000 tonnes.
Soymeal also closed higher in the nearby contracts with the soy complex boosted by a bullish estimate from a private analytical firm.
Traders said Farmers Commodities Corp's estimate for 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.37 billion bushels fueled the advances. The market was expecting a 2.4 billion bushel estimate.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, down from 13,872 Monday. Soymeal volume was at 16,000 contracts, down from 19,154 Monday.
Soyoil closed 0.08 cent per lb higher to 0.05 lower, with December up 0.08 at 22.82. Soymeal was $1.90 per ton higher to $0.70 lower, with December up $1.90 at $220.40.
